instructions: Tables in a Microsoft Fabric lakehouse/warehouse → a GraphQL API with inferred keys and relationships, plus Rayfin connector entities. Start with list_workspaces (or list_sources if you know the workspace), then plan_backend (nothing is deployed; it also suggests composite keys), sample_rows when a column's meaning is unclear, validate_plan to check keys and relationships against the rows (create_backend does not run it, and has no dry run), then create_backend. Before query_graphql, describe_backend gives the exact field names. Every inferred key/relationship carries the rule that produced it (K0–K5, R0–R4, or "SAP pack" for SAP tables such as VBAK/VBAP, whose keys with MANDT and order-to-cash relationships come from public sources; sap_pack_draft shows what the pack recognises and what is missing); ambiguous columns are reported, never guessed. From the same plan, without creating anything: semantic_model_draft (a Power BI model in TMDL, Direct Lake) when a report is the goal; join_path when the user asks how two tables connect or wants the SQL for it; data_dictionary for hand-over documentation; dbt_schema when the team tests with dbt; plan_drift before re-running create_backend on an existing API, to see what would change. One plan, five Fabric pieces: create_backend (the API for GraphQL), create_semantic_model (a Power BI semantic model item from the TMDL draft), create_ontology (a Fabric IQ ontology item: entity types with keys, relationship types, bindings), create_views (wide T-SQL views in a schema of their own on the SQL endpoint), create_data_agent (a Fabric data agent with the plan as instructions and examples) — all but create_backend answer with what they would create until dry_run=false. Creating a semantic model, ontology, data agent, notebook or pipeline needs a permission the operator may not have granted the app; without it the tool answers kind consent naming the scope, and the dry run still works. app_starter gives a Lovable prompt, connection details, queries and the Supabase edge function for an app on a created API; app_readiness lists what that API still needs before an app can use it (introspection, permissions, keys, relationships) with the next step per item. lineage shows which GraphQL APIs, semantic models, views and data agents in the workspace build on a source's tables and what a change to one table reaches; plan_drift names those objects for the tables and columns a re-run would drop. analyze_schema reads an unknown lakehouse as a graph (table roles, central tables, subject areas, cycles, which relationships can be active); suggest_relationships when the plan lacks links: it ranks candidate columns and checks the best against the data, suggesting only. From understanding to building: silver_notebook_draft and create_silver_notebook give a Fabric PySpark notebook that writes de-duplicated silver tables with every reference checked and a quarantine table, never over the source; drift_monitor_draft and create_drift_monitor a nightly notebook and pipeline that compare the plan with the last one and message a webhook; answer_query_draft turns a question (Swedish or English) into T-SQL over the safest join path, or GraphQL for an existing API, and query_graphql with question= runs it. gold_views_draft and create_gold_views give materialized lake views over the silver tables, one wide view per fact table with the plan's keys and relationships as data quality rules; compare_semantic_model checks an existing Power BI semantic model against the plan (missing, contradicted, cardinality, direction, active); export_item_definitions gives what the creating tools would create as files in Fabric's Git format, for the user's own repository. Columns that look like personal data by name are masked in sample_rows and left out of drafted queries and gold views unless show_personal_data=true. Alongside Microsoft's own Fabric MCP servers (Fabric Core and the local Fabric MCP Server for workspaces, items and files; Fabric IQ MCP for questions to semantic models; Power BI Modeling MCP for editing a model), this server is the part that works out how the tables relate and builds from that plan. This server reads Microsoft Fabric only; a Databricks adapter (Draft only: Unity Catalog, informational constraints, a Lakeflow pipeline, metric views) runs in the local stdio server, see /docs#databricks-draft-only. A call that cannot be completed answers with error (plain words), kind (a stable code such as not_found, no_access, capacity, sign_in, consent, schema_not_found, timeout, rate_limited with retry_after) and hint (the next step that fixes it). Five first questions that pay off on a lakehouse nobody has documented: (1) analyze_schema — which tables are facts, which are dimensions, what are the subject areas; (2) plan_backend — the keys and relationships with the rule behind each; (3) validate_plan — are the keys unique and do the references hold; (4) suggest_relationships — which columns look like references but are in no relationship; (5) data_dictionary — the hand-over document with everything above. review_plan keeps the plan, the decisions about it and the checks as a file for the user's own repository; passed back as previous it applies the decisions again and marks checks on changed tables stale. Shared parameters: workspace (list_workspaces), source (list_sources; lakehouse, warehouse or SQL database) and api take a name or an id; confirmed lists relationships the user confirmed and is not an approval flag; an entry has source, source_cols, target, target_cols (default source_cols) and optional field_name and reverse_name; tables narrows what is shown or included while the plan is still made from the whole schema. Test status: on 27 October 2026 every tool but sap_pack_draft, create_ontology, create_silver_notebook, create_drift_monitor and create_gold_views ran from Claude against a Fabric workspace with synthetic data, read-only or as a draft, and create_views and create_data_agent as dry runs (compare_semantic_model only as far as the model lookup; create_backend only as an update in place of shop_api with confirmed); no new item was created, so creating a new one is unit-tested only (status per tool: /docs#test-status).

annotations.title: Create or update the GraphQL API

tools.description:
Creates a Fabric API for GraphQL item over the source's tables with the plan's keys and relationships, or updates
the API of that name in place. Requires workspace, source and name. Returns JSON {summary, result, card
(endpoint, portal steps left), skipped_relationships}. Changes Fabric: an update replaces the API's definition;
tables outside `tables` or gone from the source leave it, field names of unchanged relationships are kept, and
no item is deleted. When an update would drop relationships the API has, nothing is written and the answer (kind
would_remove) lists them as confirmed entries. No dry run, and it does not run validate_plan; plan_backend
proposes, validate_plan checks, plan_drift previews an update. Errors: {error, kind, hint}.
